chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele and activates CCAT2 to promote colorectal cancer

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt T allele. TCF7L2 has HCT116 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant (E05) and is highly expressed in HCT116. TCF7L2 has no own QBiC-SELEX model in this evidence set, so the mapped LEF1 row is not used as own-model allelic evidence. The ref>alt direction is inferred from the literature linking rs6983267/8q24 to allele-specific TCF7L2 binding (E37) and from the CCAT2-TCF7L2-MYC literature (E37a), not from an own-model QBiC measurement.

The variant lies in proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447 with DNase and H3K27ac signal, and TCF7L2 occupancy overlaps this element in HCT116 (E03, E04, E05). The ENCODE z-scores are maxima over biosamples, so the HCT116-specific chromatin state is inferred from the HCT116 ChIP context rather than directly stated in E03.

CCAT2 is directly overlapped by the variant (E01), and literature places CCAT2 as a TCF7L2 regulator and enhancer of MYC/Wnt with allele-specific features at rs6983267 (E37a, E37b). No CCAT2 eQTL in colon or HCT116 is provided, so this gene link is literature- and overlap-based rather than expression-QTL-based.
HCT116 colorectal cancer cells have open chromatin context at the variant and TCF7L2 occupancy over it (E04, E05).

The locus is associated with colorectal cancer (E15). Several E15 CRC records report G as the effect allele (colorectal cancer or advanced adenoma p 3.0e-64; colon polyps; PheCode 153.2), while the strongest CRC record reports T (p 2.0e-122), so the risk-allele direction is not fully resolved. If G is the risk allele, stronger TCF7L2 binding on G raising CCAT2 and downstream MYC/Wnt is a coherent mechanism (E37a).

predictions: The G allele shows stronger TCF7L2 occupancy at chr8:127401060 in HCT116.
The G allele gives higher CCAT2 expression in colorectal cells.
falsified_if: No allele-specific TCF7L2 occupancy is detected at the variant.
CCAT2 expression is not allele-specific or not TCF7L2-responsive in colorectal cells.
G is not the colorectal cancer risk allele in the relevant colorectal context.

chains.title: SRF binds the ref G allele and represses POU5F1B at the 8q24 enhancer

links.claim: SRF binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt T allele. SRF has HCT116 ENCODE ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant (E09) and an own QBiC-SELEX model showing ref>alt binding above the gate (z -7.74, effect -1.191; E20), with SRF expressed in HCT116 (25.61 TPM; E20). QBiC-SELEX is in vitro, so allele-specific occupancy in HCT116 remains a prediction.

The variant lies in proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447 with DNase and H3K27ac signal, and active-element ChIP factors are present over the element in HCT116 (E03, E04). E03 z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not HCT116-specific.

POU5F1B has a colon transverse eQTL in which the alt T allele increases expression (NES +0.20; E17) and is TWAS-implicated in colorectal cancer (E18b); POU5F1B is also oncogenic in CRC models (E18c, E18d). The L2G score of 0.89 is driven mainly by prostate-cancer and PSA credible sets, not CRC, and no chromatin contact in HCT116 links this element to POU5F1B.
HCT116 colorectal cancer cells have open chromatin context at the variant and SRF occupancy over it (E04, E09).

The strongest CRC GWAS record reports T as the effect allele (E15), and the T allele raises POU5F1B in colon transverse (E17); POU5F1B is oncogenic (E18d). This chain therefore requires SRF to repress POU5F1B so that loss of SRF binding on T raises POU5F1B and risk. Other E15 CRC records report G as the effect allele, so the risk-allele direction is not fully resolved.

predictions: The G allele shows stronger SRF occupancy at chr8:127401060 in HCT116.
POU5F1B expression is higher on the T allele if SRF represses POU5F1B.
SRF knockdown increases POU5F1B expression in colorectal cells.
falsified_if: No allele-specific SRF occupancy is detected at the variant.
POU5F1B expression is not higher on the T allele in colorectal cells.
SRF acts as an activator rather than a repressor at this element.

chains.title: SP1 binds the ref G allele and activates CASC8 at the 8q24 enhancer

links.claim: SP1 binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt T allele, but this allelic claim is weak. SP1 has HCT116 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant (E06), but its own QBiC-SELEX model is below the gate (effect -0.169, z -3.04; E36), and the gate-passing row is a CIS-BP-mapped SP4 model rather than an SP1 own-model measurement. I therefore treat the allelic direction as weak, occupancy-supported but not established.
The variant lies in pELS EH38E3858447 with enhancer chromatin marks, and SP1 occupancy overlaps the element in HCT116 (E03, E04, E06). E03 z-scores are maxima over biosamples.

The variant is an intronic CASC8 variant (E01), and CASC8 has a significant whole-blood eQTL where the alt T allele decreases expression (NES -0.32; E17). No colon or HCT116 CASC8 eQTL or chromatin-contact evidence links this element to CASC8.
HCT116 colorectal cancer cells have open chromatin context at the variant and SP1 occupancy over it (E04, E06).

This chain requires T to be the colorectal cancer risk allele and SP1 to activate CASC8, with lower CASC8 increasing risk. The T-risk direction is supported by the strongest CRC record but contradicted by several other E15 CRC records with G as effect allele, and no evidence supports a protective role for CASC8.

predictions: The G allele shows stronger SP1 occupancy at chr8:127401060 in HCT116.
CASC8 expression is higher on the G allele and lower on the T allele.
falsified_if: No allele-specific SP1 occupancy is detected at the variant.
CASC8 expression does not track the SP1-bound allele.
SP1 knockdown does not affect CASC8 expression.

grades_v0.reason: E09/E20 give HCT116 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant (ENCSR000BSC) for SRF plus an own-model QBiC-SELEX change above gate in the stated direction (ref>alt, z -7.74, effect -1.191), with SRF expressed at 25.6 TPM. Both required halves are present and directionally concordant. Caveat: SELEX is in vitro only, so allele-specific occupancy in HCT116 remains a prediction.

E03 places the variant inside pELS EH38E3858447 with DNase/H3K27ac signal and E04 shows HCT116 ChIP peaks over it, including active-element cofactors (EP300, Pol II-associated factors). Caveat that z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not HCT116-specific.

E17 is a direct variant-to-POU5F1B eQTL (Colon_Transverse, alt T NES +0.20, p 8.2e-6) and E18b TWAS-implicates POU5F1B, but E16's L2G 0.89 is dominated by prostate-cancer GWAS credible sets, not CRC, and nothing shows this element contacts POU5F1B (78.9 kb, gene body) in HCT116. The specific claim 'this enhancer regulates POU5F1B' is therefore indirect.
E04 shows open chromatin/HCT116 ChIP peaks at the variant and E09/E20 show SRF occupancy in HCT116 itself; the element and the TF are documented in the stated cell type.

E15 does report T as the CRC effect allele in the strongest record (p 2e-122), but the mechanistic half (SRF represses POU5F1B) has no cited support - no knockdown, reporter or allele-specific assay - and E15 itself contains CRC-relevant records with effect allele G (colorectal cancer or advanced adenoma p 3e-64; colon polyps; PheCode 153.2). The risk-allele direction is not consistently T.

Occupancy is solid (E06, HCT116 peak ENCSR000BSF), but the allelic SELEX evidence is not SP1's own model: E21 uses a CIS-BP-mapped SP4 model, i.e. a related TF's binding change standing in for SP1, with a small effect (-0.211) and a large drop in predicted site strength (95.8th to 75.9th percentile). Mapped-model evidence for a different (paralogous) factor does not establish an SP1-specific allelic change.
Same as H1: E03 pELS containing the variant with enhancer marks; E04 active-element occupancy in HCT116.

E17 gives a CASC8 eQTL but in Whole_Blood (NES -0.32), not colon or HCT116, and CASC8 is an intronic lncRNA overlapping the variant rather than a demonstrated target of this element; no chromatin contact or reporter links the element to CASC8 in the relevant cell type.
E04/HCT116 peaks plus E06 HCT116 SP1 peak establish open chromatin and SP1 occupancy in the stated cell type.

Requires both that T is the CRC risk allele (contradicted by several E15 records with effect allele G) and that SP1 activates CASC8 with CASC8 lowering risk - neither the activation direction nor a protective role for CASC8 is supported by any cited evidence.

Occupancy is present (E05, HCT116 ENCSR000EUV; 63.6 TPM), but the allelic change comes from a CIS-BP-mapped LEF1 model (E22, z -4.66, effect -0.47), not an own TCF7L2 model; TCF7L2 is only covered through mapped models, so the direction is inferred from a paralog's binding profile.
E03 places the variant in pELS EH38E3858447 and E05 shows a TCF7L2 HCT116 peak overlapping the same element.

The only cited evidence is E02, distance to TSS (334.4 kb upstream). No eQTL, chromatin contact, CRISPR or reporter evidence in the case links this variant to MYC; the chain itself concedes that direct MYC eQTL evidence is absent. Proximity alone does not bear on the claim.
E04 open chromatin plus E05 TCF7L2 occupancy in HCT116 establish the cell-type context for the element and TF.

GWAS association of the locus with CRC is strong, but the chain's phenotype link depends on an unsupported repression of MYC by TCF7L2 and on T being the risk allele (E15 is internally inconsistent), and there is no variant-to-MYC expression evidence in any tissue.

grades_final.reason: E05 gives HCT116 TCF7L2 ChIP occupancy over the variant and expression, but no TCF7L2 own-model QBiC-SELEX allele-specific measurement is used; E22 is a LEF1-mapped model and the chain itself declines it. E37/E37a do not quote allele-specific TCF7L2 binding at rs6983267, so ref>alt is inferred rather than measured.

E03 directly places the variant in pELS EH38E3858447, and E04/E05 show HCT116 occupancy, but E03 DNase/H3K27ac z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not HCT116-specific. The HCT116 enhancer state is inferred rather than directly shown.

E01 shows the variant lies in CCAT2 and E37b links rs6983267 to allele-specific CCAT2 features, but there is no colon/HCT116 CCAT2 eQTL or chromatin-contact evidence. E37a describes CCAT2 as a regulator of TCF7L2/MYC, not TCF7L2 activating CCAT2, so the directional TCF7L2->CCAT2 claim is overclaimed.

E05 and E04 provide direct HCT116 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant, including TCF7L2, supporting the claimed HCT116 colorectal cancer cell context. The H3K27ac component is not HCT116-specific, but the occupancy evidence is direct.

E15 strongly associates rs6983267 with colorectal cancer, but the strongest CRC record reports T as the effect allele while several other CRC records report G. H4 needs G as the risk allele for stronger TCF7L2 binding to increase CCAT2, so the phenotype direction is unresolved rather than supported.

E09 provides HCT116 SRF ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant, and E20 provides an SRF own-model QBiC-SELEX change above the gate with effect -1.191 (z -7.74), meaning the ref G allele binds more strongly. Occupancy and allelic direction agree.

E03 places the variant in pELS EH38E3858447 and E04 shows active-element factors in HCT116, but the E03 DNase/H3K27ac values are maxima over biosamples, not HCT116-specific. The HCT116 enhancer state is therefore indirect.

E17 gives a colon transverse eQTL where the T allele increases POU5F1B, and E18b/E18c/E18d support POU5F1B involvement in CRC, but there is no HCT116 chromatin contact and no evidence that SRF represses POU5F1B. The L2G score is driven mainly by prostate/PSA sets, not CRC.
E09 directly shows SRF ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in HCT116, and E04 shows HCT116 ChIP peaks at the element, supporting the claimed HCT116 cell context.

E15 associates the locus with CRC and the strongest record reports T as the effect allele, which is consistent with T raising POU5F1B (E17) and POU5F1B being oncogenic (E18d). However, multiple other CRC records report G, and the required SRF repression of POU5F1B is not evidenced, so the phenotype chain is not secure.

E06 gives HCT116 SP1 ChIP occupancy over the variant, but the SP1 own-model QBiC-SELEX row is below the gate (E36: effect -0.169, z -3.04). The gate-passing row is a CIS-BP-mapped SP4 model, not an SP1 own-model measurement, so allele-specific SP1 binding is not established.

E03 directly identifies pELS EH38E3858447 containing the variant, and E04/E06 show HCT116 occupancy, but the E03 DNase/H3K27ac z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not HCT116-specific. HCT116 enhancer activity is inferred.

E01 shows the variant is intronic in CASC8 and E17 gives a whole-blood CASC8 eQTL where T decreases expression, but there is no colon or HCT116 CASC8 eQTL and no chromatin-contact evidence linking the SP1-bound element to CASC8. The gene link is indirect and tissue-mismatched.
E06 directly shows SP1 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in HCT116, and E04 provides HCT116 ChIP peaks at the element, supporting the claimed HCT116 colorectal cancer cell context.

E15 associates the locus with CRC, but the effect allele is inconsistent across CRC records (T strongest, G in multiple others). The chain also requires T risk with lower CASC8 increasing risk, and no evidence supports CASC8 as protective or SP1 activating CASC8 in colorectal cells.

Determines whether SP1 has its own QBiC-SELEX model at this variant or is only covered through the CIS-BP-mapped SP4 model used in E21; if only mapped, the H2 binding link stays weak, if an own model agrees in direction it becomes supported.

In the post-GWAS analyses, we first identified new genome-wide significant associations: three genomic risk loci were identified at 8q24.21 (rs6983267, P = 6.98 × 10-12), 15q13.3 (rs58658771, P = 1.40 × 10-10), and 18q21.1 (rs6507874, P = 1.91 × 10-14).

Here, upon characterizing cancer-specific transposable element-driven transpochimeric gene transcripts (TcGTs) produced by this tumor in the SYSCOL cohort, we find that expression of the hominid-restricted retrogene POU5F1B through aberrant activation of a primate-specific endogenous retroviral promoter is a strong negative prognostic biomarker.

The definitory mechanisms of CCAT2 are its role as a regulator of the TCF7L2 transcription factor, enhancer of MYC expression, and activator of the WNT/β-catenin pathway, as well as a role in promoting and maintaining chromosome instability through the BOP1-AURKB pathway.

Additionally, we highlight how the encompassing rs6983267 SNP has been shown to confer CCAT2 with allele-specific functional and structural particularities, such as the allelic-specific reprogramming of glutamine metabolism.
We demonstrate that rs6651252 resides within a Wnt responsive DNA enhancer element (WRE) and that the disease associated allele augments binding of the TCF7L2 transcription factor to this region.
Using CRISPR/Cas9 directed gene editing and epigenetic modulation, we find that the rs6651252 enhancer regulates expression of the c-MYC proto-oncogene (MYC).

However, recent studies have identified numerous tissue-specific noncoding enhancers of MYC that play major roles in cancer, highlighting long-range transcriptional regulation of MYC as a critical novel mechanism leading to MYC hyperactivation and as a potential target for new therapeutic strategies in the near future.
